existence.reason: CSE701 covers general AI applications in software engineering and mining software repositories, whereas the new course focuses specifically on AI-native software development, agentic workflows, and human-AI collaborative development processes.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course, serving as a practical, workflow-oriented complement to advanced research-focused courses like CSE701.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 investigates data-driven and research perspectives on AI in software engineering, whereas this course emphasizes practical, end-to-end agentic software development, tool use, and loop engineering.
CSE594A focuses on foundational agentic reasoning and algorithmic problem solving, whereas this course targets applied software engineering workflows and developer tool integration.
CSE582 covers product line evolution, maintenance, and legacy systems, whereas this course deals with modern AI-native development and software factories driven by coding agents.
CSE581 covers traditional systems analysis and requirements engineering theories, whereas this course focuses on spec-driven development using AI agents.
AI501 provides foundational machine learning theory, whereas this course applies evaluation and reliability concepts specifically to AI-generated software artifacts.
CSE201 teaches foundational advanced programming and object-oriented design, whereas this course builds upon those fundamentals to explore automated testing and execution via AI coding assistants.

prerequisites.justification: Students require strong programming and software engineering fundamentals, including object-oriented design and unit testing, to effectively build and evaluate agent-assisted software.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The course matters for target students by equipping them with practical skills in agentic development environments, tool use and orchestration frameworks, specification-driven development, loop engineering and execution traces, testing, evaluation, and reliability, as well as a capstone project. Students will be able to configure coding assistants, implement agent skills and tool use integrations, construct executable specifications, analyse loop engineering execution traces, evaluate reliability and automated test coverage, and assess end-to-end AI-native software development projects. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and projects.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules follow a logical progression from foundational agentic development environments and tool orchestration to specification-driven design, loop engineering, and comprehensive testing, building directly upon the software engineering fundamentals required from prerequisite course CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises quizzes, assignments, a midsem exam, an endsem exam, and a project, aligning with practical course outcomes that require both conceptual understanding and hands-on implementation of AI-native developer workflows.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701, which investigates data-driven and research perspectives, or CSE594A, which focuses on foundational agentic reasoning, this course emphasizes practical, end-to-end agentic software development, tool use, and loop engineering.
